title: D-Backs: Hazen on Trade Deadline Possibilities
text:
Diamondbacks’ Deadline Strategy Hinges on Crucial July Stretch The Arizona Diamondbacks face a pivotal July as they weigh their options for the MLB trade deadline. General Manager Mike Hazen emphasizes the importance of the next few weeks in determining whether the team will be buyers or sellers.
The Arizona Diamondbacks find themselves in a precarious position as July unfolds, teetering on the edge of contention. Currently fourth in the NL West with a 43-42 record, the team’s trajectory over the next few weeks will dictate their approach to the MLB trade deadline . General Manager Mike Hazen recently shed light on the team’s strategy, emphasizing the need for the Diamondbacks to prove they are worthy of investment.
Hazen’s Deadline Beliefs: Buy, Sell, or Hold? Speaking on “The Show” podcast, Hazen articulated a nuanced approach to the deadline. “I want this team to put us in a position to buy,” he stated, adding that the team needs to show they are “within a distance that we feel like we’re being responsible in adding to this team.” This suggests a willingness to add pieces, but only if the team demonstrates competitiveness.
The upcoming schedule is laden with opportunities for the diamondbacks to make their case. A four-game series against the San Francisco Giants,followed by matchups with the Kansas City Royals and a critical four-game set against the san Diego Padres,will provide a crucial test. The Diamondbacks will conclude this stretch against the Los Angeles Angels before the All-Star Break and begin the second half hosting the St. Louis Cardinals. Thes games pit them against several Wild Card rivals, offering a chance to directly impact their playoff positioning.
Wild Card Chase Heats Up The Diamondbacks’ recent performance has improved their standing in the Wild Card race. as of earlier this week, they were five games behind St. Louis for the final Wild Card spot. Thanks to a two-game winning streak against the Giants and losses by the Cincinnati Reds, Giants, Cardinals, Padres and New York Mets, they have shaved that deficit to just 2.5 games back of both San Diego and st. Louis.
“I want to buy really bad, but we have a responsibility to the institution too,” hazen acknowledged, underlining the need for a balanced approach. “We’ve been so up-and-down this year. We have a talented team, this team is capable of playing better. … We need to start ticking off some wins here though.”
Key Takeaway: The Diamondbacks need to demonstrate consistent winning to justify adding meaningful assets at the trade deadline. Their performance in July will be the deciding factor. Potential Trade Pieces regardless of whether they become buyers or sellers, the Diamondbacks possess valuable assets that other teams covet. They have a number of impending free agents, including Eugenio Suárez and Josh Naylor , two highly sought-after rental bats. Merrill Kelly and Zac Gallen also headline the pitching staff, though Gallen is having a subpar season. Shelby Miller and Jalen Beeks , two relievers, have also emerged as valuable trade pieces due to their strong performance and affordable salaries.
Trade Value Alert: Keep an eye on Shelby Miller and Jalen Beeks. Their performance and contract situations make them attractive options for contending teams seeking bullpen help. According to Hazen, most interest has been in the rentals. He also noted, “Talking about players (under long-term contractual control) gets into a little deeper conversation that we really haven’t had yet. Most of the initial phone calls are on the players that would be expiring.”
Bullpen Reinforcements a Priority If the Diamondbacks decide to buy, bolstering the bullpen will be a top priority. The team has suffered significant injuries,losing Justin Martinez and AJ puk to season-ending elbow surgeries. While Miller and Beeks have stepped up, the middle relief group remains a work in progress. To fill the gaps, the team has added John Curtiss , Anthony DeSclafani , and Jake Woodford on minor league deals, while rookie Kyle Backhus and veterans Kevin Ginkel and Ryan Thompson have experienced inconsistent results.
Injury Impact: The loss of Justin Martinez and AJ Puk significantly weakens the Diamondbacks’ bullpen, making reinforcements a necessity if they aim to contend. Hazen hopes to add one or two late-game arms. He referenced the acquisition of Paul Sewald in 2023 as a triumphant exmaple, noting that adding a closer or setup man would allow manager Torey Lovullo to utilize Miller and Beeks in earlier, high-leverage situations. Potential targets include established closers like David bednar and Kyle Finnegan , who are likely to be available. Other arms who may become available include Aroldis Chapman , Anthony Bender , Calvin Faucher , Seranthony Domínguez and Gregory Soto .
Ultimately, the Diamondbacks’ fate at the trade deadline hinges on their performance over the next few weeks.
